rationale: The investigator chose the cross-sectional design, and the evidence supports it: the safety of longer intervals has randomised and cohort answers (claim c3), while the unknown is how intervals are set now (claim c1), how reliable the risk record is (claim c2) and who has no interval (claim c4). A record sample from all 14 practices in one month measures that directly within six months of part-time research time.
alternatives: Two-year cohort of decay by interval (not chosen: repeats randomised evidence and needs follow-up funding)
Questionnaire to dentists (refused: reports intentions, not recorded practice)
whyNotMoreComplex: Linking to later decay would answer a safety question already studied; the commissioners need a baseline of current practice.

decision.statement: Measure how recall intervals are set in the 14 practices with a cross-sectional study of records: 80 adult records per practice from one month, comparing each interval with the recorded risk category and with independent risk markers, and reporting missing intervals by deprivation.
decision.question: Is recall in the network's practices risk-based, and for whom is it not?

criteria.text: Routine recall is often not risk-based and risk fields are unreliable, so a direct local measure is needed.
Missing intervals concentrate in deprived areas and must be reported.
The safety of longer intervals is still unknown, which would favour the cohort design instead.

gates.requirement: Governance confirmation that anonymised record extracts need no research ethics review
gates.evidence: Network governance note PBRN-GOV-2026-11 dated 2026-07-30, supplied by the investigator

gates.requirement: Signed data release agreements from all 14 practices
gates.evidence: Eleven of 14 signed by 2026-09-15 (investigator's local fact)

alternatives: A two-year cohort of patients by interval (the investigator's second option)
A questionnaire to dentists about how they set intervals
decision.note: Rests on ledger claims c1, c2 and c4; c3 supports the defeating criterion being unmet. Three practices have not yet signed data release agreements.

summary: Cross-sectional record study recommended in line with the investigator's choice; one gate is unmet until all practices sign.
